top_signals.title: Valterra Platinum Bets on Underground Mining Project
top_signals.summary: South Africa's Valterra Platinum is the world's largest miner of platinum group metals by market cap, and Valterra's Mogalakwena facility is the world's largest open-pit platinum mine. The company plans to take its operations in a new direction, tunneling down for higher-grade underground ore with a project called Sandsloot. On Bloomberg Chief Future Officer, Valterra Platinum CFO Sayurie Naidoo tells Jennifer Zabasajja why the underground extension is a perfect fit with the company's "value over volume" strategy. (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Commodity repricing impacting inflation expectations and industrial supply chains.

top_signals.title: Valterra CFO Guides Market Development Investments
top_signals.summary: Platinum group metals (PGMs) are primarily used for catalytic converters in internal combustion engines. So as ICE vehicles are phased out in favor of battery electric vehicles, PGM miners are seeking new markets and applications for their products. On Bloomberg Chief Future Officer, CFO Sayurie Naidoo and CEO Craig Miller tell Jennifer Zabasajja how Valterra Platinum's finance and marketing teams are evaluating investments in new market development. (Source: Bloomberg)

top_signals.title: SK Hynix’s 57% Drop From Peak Shows Rapid Unwind of AI Excesses
top_signals.summary: A global selloff in semiconductor stocks has dragged shares of SK Hynix Inc. down 57% from their peak four months ago, underscoring the scale of an investor exodus from the frothiest corners of the AI trade.

top_signals.title: The Mecca Pact and Pakistan’s Bid to Become Indispensable
top_signals.summary:
For most of its history, Pakistan’s geopolitical value has risen and fallen with other countries’ emergencies. The Mecca Pact may be its most serious attempt yet to break that cycle. On Aug. 31, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey established a secretariat in Saudi Arabia for the Mecca Defence Agreement. The first secretary-general comes from Pakistan for a three-year term. The agreement builds on the Saudi-Pakistani agreement signed in September 2025, locking a decades-old informal security arrangement into a mutual defense pact. top_signals.title: U.S. Soldier Gets 70 Months in Prison for AT&T, Verizon Extortions
top_signals.summary: A U.S. Army soldier who pleaded guilty to hacking into multiple telecommunications companies and stealing mobile call and text metadata for more than 100 million AT&T customers in 2024 was sentenced to 70 months in federal prison today and ordered to pay nearly $300,000 in restitution to victims.
